Subject: Dedicated pool questionnaire - throughput targets and GPU mix

Camila,

Thanks for taking our call earlier. As we assemble our RFP package, procurement asked us to collect a short, concrete questionnaire about how Redwood would recommend sizing a dedicated pool for our primary inference workload (clinical summarization + semantic search). The key constraints: peak QPS ~600 requests/min (90th percentile, bursts up to 1,200), median generated tokens per request ~120, worst-case 1,024, and a P99 latency goal of 200ms for summarization (we can tolerate higher latency for embeddings/reranking).

Could you confirm the following and return as one PDF/attachment:
- Recommended GPU SKU mix (e.g., A100-80GB vs H100-80GB or NVLink nodes) for predictable 24/7 baseline with a separate burst lane.
- Throughput targets per GPU (tokens/sec and requests/min) for the summarization model (we plan to use a 13B open checkpoint).
- Suggested reservation commitment (baseline vs burst buffer) and fallback policy if burst capacity is consumed.
- Any caveats around KV cache sizing, sequence-length impact, and batching assumptions you made.

We need this consolidated into the vendor responses section by EOD Fri (2027-03-05). Can you also attach any modeling spreadsheet you used?

Best,
Morgan
Morgan Lee
Lead Procurement Analyst, Asterion Health

Morgan —

Thanks, that’s very clear. I attached a short write-up plus our internal modeling workbook (redwood-gpu-blend-modeling.xlsx) and a draft SLA appendix (draft-sla-burst-lanes.pdf). High level notes below; the attached spreadsheet contains the per-GPU throughput rows and the conservative assumptions used.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Baseline: H100-80GB nodes are the recommended baseline for 24/7 predictable throughput for your 13B summarization model when targeting P99~200ms for 120-token median requests. H100 provides better single-stream latency and sustained token throughput for mixed sequence lengths.
- Burst lane: We recommend a separate burst pool mixing H100 + A100-80GB (if available at your preferred region) sized to absorb 2x your 90th percentile burst (~2,400 requests/min) for short windows (minutes). The burst lane uses our autoscale + prewarmed containers to hit peak quickly.
- Per-GPU throughput (conservative): H100-80GB approx 9,500 tokens/sec when using continuous batching with avg seq 120; A100-80GB ~7,200 tokens/sec (numbers in workbook). For request-count mapping, assume ~120 tokens/request => H100 ~79 reqs/sec (~4,740 reqs/min) sustained in ideal batching; practical conservative capacity ~60% of that for mixed traffic and latency SLOs.
- Reservation recommendation: Baseline commit to capacity covering your 90th percentile sustained load (~600 reqs/min) with a burst buffer sized for 1,800–2,400 reqs/min depending on your preferred cost/SLA tradeoff. Attach shows 3 scenarios (cost-optimized, balanced, high-availability).
- Fallback policy: If burst lane exhausted, traffic can be routed to lower-cost A100 pool with noted latency uplift and token throttling. We can bake automatic fallback rules with priority routing and token-level shedding to protect baseline.
- KV cache & batching caveats: Larger KV caches (per-request context >2k tokens) reduce batching efficiency; we modeled worst-case 1,024 token sequences in the workbook which reduces per-GPU effective tokens/sec by ~30%. We call out shard sizes and prewarmed KV cache warmup windows in the attachment.

I’ll loop Steph and Karthik for any technical clarifications before we send the final PDF back to you.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Steph / Camila —

Short answer: yes, we can recommend a prewarmed standby lane for deterministic response, with a few conservative constraints to call out in the RFP:
- Guarantee window: we can guarantee a 3-minute fully prewarmed window at 2,400 reqs/min with a 30% cost uplift relative to the committed baseline (workbook scenario B). Longer guaranteed windows are possible but cost rises linearly with reserved instances.
- Warmup mechanics: the prewarm is achieved via hot containers + KV cache priming; if there’s a failover to cold autoscale we expect a 90–180s additional P99 penalty while KV cache warms per-shard.
- SKU blending note: mixing H100 & A100 in the same burst policy is fine but must be explicit about traffic routing priorities — H100 gets latency-sensitive traffic, A100 is for background inference and reranking.
- Monitoring hooks: include token-level dashboards and an automated rollback if P99 crosses 300ms for >2 consecutive windows.

I recommend we present the balanced scenario (scenario B) to Asterion with explicit numbers: baseline commit = 2x H100 nodes (config in workbook), prewarm lane = 4x H100 + 2x A100 for 3-minute guarantee. I attached a short snippet to the workbook.

-karthik
